title: The Last Salt Revisited
premise: Mirabel Lockridge makes his living stealing memories from the salt-merchants of Thornfell, selling them back to the forgetful and the grieving. When a child named Oren arrives speaking the dead tongue of the Salt Covenant — the ancient pact that once bound the human realms to the memory-eating deep — Mirabel learns the memories he has been stealing are fragments of the covenant itself, and that his own stolen childhood holds its final clause. Hunted by the usurper Vane Corvess, who feeds on forgotten oaths to raise an army of the oath-broken, Mirabel and Oren must cross Thornfell to reach the free cities and restore the covenant before the last salt road dissolves. In the end, Mirabel chooses truth over the comfortable lies he has built his identity on, sacrificing his stolen memories — including his knowledge of who he truly is — to reforge the pact, and wakes with nothing but Oren's hand in his and a name he must earn again.
about_author: D. M. Dunmore is the pen name of a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing smugglers' ledgers in coastal trading towns before turning to fiction. They write about memory, debt, and the bargains people make with places.

chapters.title: The Taste of Borrowed Years
chapters.summary: POV Mirabel. On a rain-slicked night in the salt-town of Greyharbor, Mirabel lifts a memory of a dead daughter from a grieving merchant and sells it to a rival, showing the mechanics and moral cost of his trade. The emotional beat is uneasy competence: he is very good at something that quietly hollows him out.

chapters.title: The Child at the Door
chapters.summary: POV Mirabel. Oren appears at Mirabel's safehouse, speaking a language that makes the salt in the room crystallize, and the words land in Mirabel like memories he never lived. When Corvess's oath-breakers burn the district searching for the child, Mirabel flees with him into Thornfell. The beat is reluctant responsibility hardening into resolve.

chapters.title: What the Mountain Remembers
chapters.summary: POV Oren. Through the child's alien perception, the Thornfell passes are revealed as fossilized memory — every smuggler's road a forgotten promise made solid. Oren recognizes Mirabel's thief-craft as a corrupted form of covenant-keeping. The beat is wonder shadowed by dread as Corvess's army enters the mountains behind them.

chapters.title: The Ferryman's Ledger
chapters.summary: POV Mirabel. At a river crossing, the ferrywoman Brannoc holds an old debt against the Lockridge name and demands payment in memory. Mirabel pays with a cherished one and learns, from her ledger, that his family were once covenant-wardens — traitors to their own office. The beat is the first crack in his identity.

chapters.title: An Army of the Unkept
chapters.summary: POV Oren. Corvess's vanguard catches them at the pass of Hollow Vows: soldiers who have sold their own memories for strength, faceless and tireless. Mirabel's stolen memories let him walk among them unnoticed, but Oren sees what it costs him to pretend. The beat is terror braided with the first true trust between them.

chapters.title: The Usurper's Offer
chapters.summary: POV Mirabel. Captured and brought before Corvess, Mirabel is offered his stolen childhood back — complete, painless — if he surrenders Oren and the covenant's final clause. Corvess reveals the clause names a warden's heir. The beat is temptation at its most intimate: the self he could recover versus the child he has promised to protect.

chapters.title: Salt in the Wound
chapters.summary: POV Oren. Oren breaks them out using the covenant-tongue to unmake the fortress's founding oath, an act that ages him years in a single night and reveals he is not truly a child but a covenant-spirit wearing one. Mirabel must decide whether the loyalty he feels is to the boy or to the lie of the boy. The beat is grief for a friendship built on a partial truth.

chapters.title: The Road the Free Cities Forgot
chapters.summary: POV Mirabel. Fleeing through a dissolving salt road, Mirabel gives Oren fragments of his stolen memories so the child-spirit can hold the way open, and in giving them up Mirabel begins to remember his own past unbidden. The free cities appear below, but so does Corvess's host. The beat is bittersweet clarity: he cannot save the boy, the road, and himself.

chapters.title: The Reforging
chapters.summary: POV Mirabel and Oren, alternating. In the covenant-chamber beneath the free cities, Corvess arrives to claim the clause for himself. The final clause requires a warden's willing sacrifice of all held memory. Mirabel speaks the old tongue with Oren guiding him, and Corvess, denied the clause, is unmade by every oath he has broken. The beat is the climax: truth chosen over self at the point of no return.

chapters.title: A Name Worth Keeping
chapters.summary: POV Mirabel. Memoryless, Mirabel wakes in Greyharbor as a stranger, with Oren — restored to his true form, no longer a child — keeping watch. The covenant holds, the roads are whole, and Oren offers him a single memory to start from: the night a child knocked on his door. Mirabel declines it, choosing to earn his life instead. The beat is quiet, earned hope.
